# CLI Reference



The `jen` CLI provides commands for development, building, and running your application.

Usage [#usage]

```bash
jen <command> [options]
```

Commands [#commands]

`jen dev` [#jen-dev]

Start the development server with hot module replacement.

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

* Powered by Vite with HMR
* Streaming SSR for all routes
* API route support
* Middleware execution
* Runs on the port specified in `jen.config.ts` (default: 3000)

***

`jen build` [#jen-build]

Generate a static site from all non-dynamic routes.

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen build
    npx jen build --adapter=vercel
    npx jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen build
    pnpm jen build --adapter=vercel
    pnpm jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen build
    yarn jen build --adapter=vercel
    yarn jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen build
    bunx jen build --adapter=vercel
    bunx jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

| Flag                   | Description                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `--adapter=vercel`     | Generate Vercel Build Output API structure |
| `--adapter=cloudflare` | Generate Cloudflare Worker bundle          |

Outputs to `dist/static/` by default. Includes `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`.

***

`jen start` [#jen-start]

Build and start a production-hardened server.

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen start
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen start
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen start
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen start
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

* Runs the full SSG build first
* Starts the production HTTP server
* NIST/OWASP security headers enabled
* ISR cache management active

***

Display system and framework diagnostics.

# Configuration



Customize Jen.js behavior by creating a `jen.config.ts` (or `.js`, `.mjs`) file in your project root.

Basic Example [#basic-example]

```typescript title="jen.config.ts"
import type { JenConfig } from 'we-jenjs/types';

export default {
  port: 3000,
  buildDirectory: 'dist/static',
  name: 'My App',
} satisfies Partial<JenConfig>;
```

Full Reference [#full-reference]

```typescript
interface JenConfig {
  port: number;                    // Dev/production server port (default: 3000)
  buildDirectory: string;          // Static output directory (default: 'dist/static')
  name?: string;                   // Application name (default: 'Jen.js App')

  middleware?: {
    enabled?: boolean;             // Enable middleware pipeline (default: true)
    cors?: boolean | Record<string, unknown>;      // CORS config
    bodyParser?: boolean | Record<string, unknown>; // Body parsing
    errorBoundary?: boolean;       // Error boundary (default: true)
    requestLogger?: boolean;       // Request logging (default: true)
    custom?: Array<{
      name: string;
      handler: (context: unknown, next: () => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>;
      priority?: number;
    }>;
  };

  isr?: {
    enabled?: boolean;             // Enable ISR (default: false)
    cacheDir?: string;             // Cache directory (default: '.cache/isr')
    maxRetries?: number;           // Max regeneration retries (default: 3)
    retryDelay?: number;           // Retry delay in ms (default: 1000)
    globalRevalidate?: number;     // Global TTL fallback in seconds
  };

  i18n?: {
    locales: string[];             // Supported locales (e.g. ['en', 'fr'])
    defaultLocale: string;         // Default locale
  };

  requireDangerouslySetScripts?: boolean; // Require <Script> opt-in (default: true)
}
```

Defaults [#defaults]

When no config file is provided, Jen.js uses these defaults:

| Option                         | Default         |
| ------------------------------ | --------------- |
| `port`                         | `3000`          |
| `buildDirectory`               | `'dist/static'` |
| `name`                         | `'Jen.js App'`  |
| `middleware.enabled`           | `true`          |
| `middleware.cors`              | `false`         |
| `middleware.errorBoundary`     | `true`          |
| `middleware.requestLogger`     | `true`          |
| `isr.enabled`                  | `false`         |
| `isr.cacheDir`                 | `'.cache/isr'`  |
| `isr.maxRetries`               | `3`             |
| `isr.retryDelay`               | `1000`          |
| `requireDangerouslySetScripts` | `true`          |

Config Loading [#config-loading]

Configuration is loaded once at startup by the `ConfigLoader`. Nested objects like `middleware` and `isr` are deep-merged with defaults — you only need to specify the values you want to override.


# Internationalization



Jen.js supports native internationalization (i18n) with automatic locale routing, `<html lang>` injection, and per-locale static builds.

Configuration [#configuration]

Enable i18n in `jen.config.ts`:

```typescript title="jen.config.ts"
export default {
  i18n: {
    locales: ['en', 'fr', 'de'],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
  },
};
```

Locale Routing [#locale-routing]

With i18n enabled, routes automatically support locale prefixes:

| URL         | Locale         | Page                  |
| ----------- | -------------- | --------------------- |
| `/en/about` | `en`           | `pages/about/app.tsx` |
| `/fr/about` | `fr`           | `pages/about/app.tsx` |
| `/about`    | `en` (default) | `pages/about/app.tsx` |

The framework intercepts requests and:

1. Extracts the first path segment
2. Matches it against `i18n.locales`
3. Strips the locale prefix before routing
4. Injects `x-jen-locale` into the request context

Accessing the Locale [#accessing-the-locale]

The current locale is available as `pageProps.locale` in your component:

```tsx title="pages/app.tsx"
export default function Home({ locale }: { locale: string }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>{locale === 'fr' ? 'Bienvenue' : 'Welcome'}</h1>
    </div>
  );
}
```

HTML Lang Injection [#html-lang-injection]

Jen.js automatically sets the `<html lang="...">` attribute during SSR based on the detected locale:

```html
<!-- Request to /fr/about -->
<html lang="fr">
```

Static Generation with i18n [#static-generation-with-i18n]

During `jen build`, pages are generated for **every configured locale**:

```
dist/static/
├── en/
│   ├── index.html
│   └── about.html
└── fr/
    ├── index.html
    └── about.html
```

Each HTML file has the correct `lang` attribute and receives `locale` as a page prop during rendering.

Translation Pattern [#translation-pattern]

Use a lightweight dictionary pattern for translations:

```tsx title="pages/app.tsx"
const translations = {
  en: { greeting: 'Hello', description: 'Welcome to our site' },
  fr: { greeting: 'Bonjour', description: 'Bienvenue sur notre site' },
};

export default function Home({ locale }: { locale: string }) {
  const t = translations[locale as keyof typeof translations] || translations.en;

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>{t.greeting}</h1>
      <p>{t.description}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# Introduction



**Jen.js** is a modern, full-stack web framework designed for speed. It combines [Bun](https://bun.sh) as the runtime, [Vite](https://vite.dev) as the bundler, [Preact](https://preactjs.com) for UI rendering, and [Rust/WASM](https://www.rust-lang.org) for critical-path routing — delivering a **3 kB** client runtime with streaming server-side rendering out of the box.

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash title="Install"
    npm install we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash title="Install"
    pnpm add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash title="Install"
    yarn add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash title="Install"
    bun add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Key Features [#key-features]

| Feature                             | Description                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Streaming SSR**                   | `renderToReadableStream` with `TransformStream` pipeline for fast TTFB             |
| **Static Site Generation**          | Pre-render all routes to static HTML at build time                                 |
| **Incremental Static Regeneration** | Stale-while-revalidate caching with configurable TTLs                              |
| **File-Based Routing**              | `pages/` directory convention with dynamic `[$param]` segments                     |
| **Nested Layouts**                  | Cascading `layout.tsx` files for persistent UI                                     |
| **Data Loaders**                    | `load()` / `server()` functions for server-side data fetching                      |
| **API Routes**                      | `pages/api/*.ts` with typed HTTP method handlers                                   |
| **Edge Middleware**                 | `middleware.ts` with `NextResponse` for redirects, rewrites, headers               |
| **SEO Metadata**                    | `export const metadata` or `generateMetadata()` per page                           |
| **i18n**                            | Locale-prefixed routing (`/en/about`, `/fr/about`) with automatic `<html lang>`    |
| **Image Optimization**              | `<Image>` component powered by Sharp with WebP conversion                          |
| **Font Optimization**               | `GoogleFont()` with automatic SSR `<head>` injection                               |
| **Script Management**               | `<Script>` with `beforeInteractive` / `afterInteractive` / `lazyOnload` strategies |
| **Edge Deployment**                 | Adapters for Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, and Node.js                               |

Architecture [#architecture]

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Client (3 kB)                                  │
│  Preact + Client Router + Hydration             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Server (Bun.serve)                             │
│  Streaming SSR · ISR · Data Loaders · API Routes│
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Build (Vite)                                   │
│  SSG · Image Optimizer · Font Injection         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Router (Rust → WASM)                           │
│  RouterMap · Pattern Matching · Route Manifest   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

What's Next? [#whats-next]

  <Card title="Routing" href="/docs/routing" />

# Installation



Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

* [Bun](https://bun.sh) v1.0 or later
* Node.js 18+ (for Vite compatibility)

Install [#install]

Add `we-jenjs` to your project:

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash title="Install"
    npm install we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash title="Install"
    pnpm add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash title="Install"
    yarn add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash title="Install"
    bun add we-jenjs
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Create Your First Page [#create-your-first-page]

Create a `pages/` directory in your project root and add a page component:

```tsx title="pages/app.tsx"
export default function Home() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Hello, Jen.js!</h1>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Start the Dev Server [#start-the-dev-server]

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">

  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen dev
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Your app is now running at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) with hot module replacement powered by Vite.

Configuration (Optional) [#configuration-optional]

Create a `jen.config.ts` file in your project root to customize behavior:

```typescript title="jen.config.ts"
import type { JenConfig } from 'we-jenjs/types';

export default {
  port: 3000,
  buildDirectory: 'dist/static',
  name: 'My App',
} satisfies Partial<JenConfig>;
```

See the [Configuration Reference](/docs/configuration) for all available options.

# Middleware



Jen.js supports a global `middleware.ts` file that intercepts every request before it reaches the router — ideal for authentication, redirects, A/B testing, and header manipulation.

Create Middleware [#create-middleware]

Add a `middleware.ts` file to your project root (next to `pages/`):

```typescript title="middleware.ts"
import { NextResponse } from 'we-jenjs';

export default function middleware(req: Request) {
  // Redirect legacy URLs
  if (new URL(req.url).pathname === '/old-page') {
    return NextResponse.redirect('/new-page');
  }

  // Continue to the router
  return NextResponse.next();
}
```

NextResponse API [#nextresponse-api]

| Method                                | Description                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NextResponse.next(init?)`            | Continue to the router (optionally with modified headers) |
| `NextResponse.redirect(url, status?)` | Redirect to a URL (default: 307)                          |
| `NextResponse.rewrite(url)`           | Internally rewrite the request to a different path        |

Redirect [#redirect]

```typescript
// Temporary redirect (307)
return NextResponse.redirect('/login');

// Permanent redirect (301)
return NextResponse.redirect('/new-url', 301);
```

Rewrite [#rewrite]

Rewrites serve content from a different path without changing the browser URL:

```typescript
// User sees /dashboard, but /app/dashboard is served
return NextResponse.rewrite('/app/dashboard');
```

Proceed with Custom Headers [#proceed-with-custom-headers]

```typescript
return NextResponse.next({
  headers: {
    'X-Custom-Header': 'value',
  },
});
```

Middleware Discovery [#middleware-discovery]

The `RouteScanner` looks for middleware files in this priority order:

1. `middleware.ts`
2. `middleware.js`
3. `middleware.tsx`
4. `middleware.jsx`

Only the first match is used.

How It Works [#how-it-works]

1. A request arrives at the server
2. If a middleware file exists, it is executed **before** the router
3. If middleware returns a `Response`, it short-circuits (no routing occurs)
4. If middleware returns via `NextResponse.next()`, the request proceeds normally

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Middleware runs on both the development server and edge adapters (Vercel Edge, Cloudflare Workers).


# Project Structure



A typical Jen.js project follows this layout:

```
my-app/
├── pages/                  # File-based routes
│   ├── app.tsx             # → /
│   ├── layout.tsx          # Root layout (wraps all pages)
│   ├── about/
│   │   └── app.tsx         # → /about
│   ├── blog/
│   │   ├── layout.tsx      # Nested layout for /blog/*
│   │   ├── app.tsx         # → /blog
│   │   └── [$slug]/
│   │       └── app.tsx     # → /blog/:slug (dynamic)
│   └── api/
│       └── users.ts        # → /api/users (API Route)
├── _app.tsx                # Global application shell (optional)
├── _error.tsx              # Custom error page (optional)
├── middleware.ts           # Edge middleware (optional)
├── jen.config.ts           # Framework configuration
└── package.json
```

Special Files [#special-files]

| File                  | Purpose                                                        |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pages/**/app.tsx`    | Page component — each resolved as a route                      |
| `pages/**/layout.tsx` | Layout component — wraps child pages in its subtree            |
| `pages/api/*.ts`      | API Route — exports HTTP method handlers (`GET`, `POST`, etc.) |
| `_app.tsx`            | Global application shell wrapping every page                   |
| `_document.tsx`       | Custom HTML document template                                  |
| `_error.tsx`          | Error boundary fallback component                              |
| `middleware.ts`       | Edge middleware interceptor (runs before routing)              |
| `jen.config.ts`       | Framework configuration file                                   |

Route Resolution [#route-resolution]

Jen.js uses a **filesystem-based router** powered by the `RouteScanner`. Each directory under `pages/` that contains an `app.tsx` (or `app.jsx`) file becomes a route:

* `pages/app.tsx` → `/`
* `pages/about/app.tsx` → `/about`
* `pages/blog/[$slug]/app.tsx` → `/blog/:slug`

Dynamic segments use the `[$paramName]` folder convention. See [Dynamic Routes](/docs/routing/dynamic-routes) for details.

Layouts [#layouts]

`layout.tsx` files are automatically discovered and nested. A layout at `pages/layout.tsx` wraps all pages, while `pages/blog/layout.tsx` wraps only pages under `/blog/*`.

See [Layouts](/docs/routing/layouts) for more details.


# SEO & Metadata



Jen.js provides a first-class Metadata API for managing page titles, descriptions, and social sharing tags — with automatic sitemap and robots.txt generation.

Static Metadata [#static-metadata]

Export a `metadata` object from any page:

```tsx title="pages/about/app.tsx"
import type { Metadata } from 'we-jenjs/types';

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'About Us',
  description: 'Learn more about our company.',
  openGraph: {
    title: 'About Us',
    siteName: 'My App',
    images: [{ url: '/og-about.png', width: 1200, height: 630 }],
  },
  twitter: {
    card: 'summary_large_image',
    site: '@myapp',
  },
};

export default function About() {
  return <h1>About Us</h1>;
}
```

Dynamic Metadata [#dynamic-metadata]

Export an async `generateMetadata()` function for data-dependent metadata:

```tsx title="pages/blog/[$slug]/app.tsx"
export async function generateMetadata(pageProps: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const post = pageProps.post as Post;
  return {
    title: post.title,
    description: post.excerpt,
    openGraph: {
      title: post.title,
      images: [{ url: post.coverImage }],
    },
  };
}
```

`generateMetadata()` receives the same props that `load()` passes to the page component.

Metadata Type [#metadata-type]

```typescript
interface Metadata {
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  openGraph?: {
    title?: string;
    description?: string;
    url?: string;
    siteName?: string;
    images?: Array<{
      url: string;
      width?: number;
      height?: number;
      alt?: string;
    }>;
    locale?: string;
    type?: string;
  };
  twitter?: {
    card?: string;
    site?: string;
    creator?: string;
  };
  robots?: string;
}
```

Automatic Sitemap & Robots [#automatic-sitemap--robots]

During `jen build`, the following files are generated automatically in `dist/static/`:

sitemap.xml [#sitemapxml]

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com</loc>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/about</loc>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

robots.txt [#robotstxt]

```
User-agent: *
Allow: /
Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
```

All non-dynamic routes discovered by the `RouteScanner` are included in the sitemap.


# GoogleFont



The `GoogleFont()` function registers optimized Google Fonts with automatic SSR `<head>` link injection.

Import [#import]

```tsx
import { GoogleFont } from 'we-jenjs';
```

Usage [#usage]

```tsx
const inter = GoogleFont('Inter', {
  weight: [400, 600, 700],
  subsets: ['latin'],
  display: 'swap',
});

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div className={inter.className} style={inter.style}>
      <h1>Hello with Inter font</h1>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Options [#options]

```typescript
interface GoogleFontOptions {
  weight?: string | number | (string | number)[];  // Font weights
  subsets?: string[];                               // e.g. ['latin', 'cyrillic']
  display?: 'auto' | 'block' | 'swap' | 'fallback' | 'optional';
}
```

Return Value [#return-value]

`GoogleFont()` returns an object for applying the font:

| Property    | Type     | Description                                   |
| ----------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | Generated CSS class (e.g. `__jen-font-inter`) |
| `variable`  | `string` | CSS custom property (e.g. `--font-inter`)     |
| `style`     | `object` | Inline style with `fontFamily` set            |
| `href`      | `string` | Google Fonts CSS URL                          |

SSR Integration [#ssr-integration]

During server-side rendering, `GoogleFont()` automatically:

1. Tracks all font URLs used on the page
2. Injects `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags into the `<head>` before flushing
3. Clears the tracked fonts after injection

This means fonts are automatically available on first render with no layout shift.

CSS Variables [#css-variables]

Use the `variable` property for CSS custom properties:

```tsx
const outfit = GoogleFont('Outfit', { weight: '400..700' });

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <div style={{ [outfit.variable]: outfit.style.fontFamily }}>
      <p style={{ fontFamily: `var(${outfit.variable})` }}>
        Variable font in action
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# <Image>



The `<Image>` component automatically optimizes local images during the build pipeline using [Sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/).

Import [#import]

```tsx
import { Image } from 'we-jenjs';
```

Usage [#usage]

```tsx
<Image
  src="/images/hero.jpg"
  alt="Hero banner"
  width={1200}
  height={630}
  quality={85}
/>
```

Props [#props]

| Prop        | Type                | Default  | Description                           |
| ----------- | ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `src`       | `string`            | —        | Image source path or external URL     |
| `alt`       | `string`            | —        | Alt text (required for accessibility) |
| `width`     | `number \| string`  | —        | Display width                         |
| `height`    | `number \| string`  | —        | Display height                        |
| `loading`   | `'lazy' \| 'eager'` | `'lazy'` | Loading strategy                      |
| `className` | `string`            | —        | CSS class name                        |
| `quality`   | `number`            | `80`     | Image quality (1–100)                 |

Automatic Optimizations [#automatic-optimizations]

* **Lazy loading** — `loading="lazy"` by default
* **Async decoding** — `decoding="async"` for non-blocking rendering
* **Aspect ratio** — Prevents CLS by setting `aspect-ratio` when `width` and `height` are provided
* **Responsive sizing** — `max-width: 100%; height: auto` applied automatically
* **Build-time processing** — Local images get `?jen-img=1&q=80` query hints for the Vite image optimizer plugin

External Images [#external-images]

External URLs (starting with `http://` or `https://`) are rendered as-is without build-time processing:

```tsx
<Image src="https://cdn.example.com/photo.jpg" alt="External photo" />
```


# <Link>



The `<Link>` component enables SPA-like navigation without full page reloads.

Import [#import]

```tsx
import { Link } from 'we-jenjs/client';
```

Usage [#usage]

```tsx
<Link href="/about">About Us</Link>
<Link href="/blog" className="nav-link">Blog</Link>
```

Props [#props]

| Prop        | Type                | Description     |
| ----------- | ------------------- | --------------- |
| `href`      | `string`            | Target URL path |
| `children`  | `ComponentChildren` | Link content    |
| `className` | `string`            | CSS class name  |
| `style`     | `JSX.CSSProperties` | Inline styles   |

How It Works [#how-it-works]

1. **Intercepts clicks** — Left-clicks without modifier keys are prevented from triggering a full navigation
2. **Updates URL** — Pushes the new path to `window.history`
3. **Dispatches event** — Fires a `jen-navigation` custom event that the client router listens for
4. **Swaps content** — The router fetches and renders the target page component without unmounting layouts

Modifier clicks (Ctrl+click, Cmd+click, etc.) fall through to the browser's native behavior, opening links in new tabs as expected.

Example [#example]

```tsx
import { Link } from 'we-jenjs/client';

export default function Navigation() {
  return (
    <nav>
      <Link href="/">Home</Link>
      <Link href="/about">About</Link>
      <Link href="/blog" className="active">Blog</Link>
    </nav>
  );
}
```


# <Script>



The `<Script>` component controls when and how third-party scripts are loaded, with built-in security.

Import [#import]

```tsx
import { Script } from 'we-jenjs';
```

Usage [#usage]

```tsx
<Script
  src="https://analytics.example.com/script.js"
  strategy="afterInteractive"
  dangerouslySetScripts
/>
```

Props [#props]

| Prop                    | Type                                                        | Default              | Description                             |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `src`                   | `string`                                                    | —                    | External script URL                     |
| `id`                    | `string`                                                    | —                    | Unique identifier (prevents duplicates) |
| `strategy`              | `'beforeInteractive' \| 'afterInteractive' \| 'lazyOnload'` | `'afterInteractive'` | Loading strategy                        |
| `dangerouslySetScripts` | `boolean`                                                   | —                    | Required security acknowledgment        |
| `children`              | `ComponentChildren`                                         | —                    | Inline script content                   |

Loading Strategies [#loading-strategies]

| Strategy            | When                               | Use Case                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `beforeInteractive` | Rendered synchronously in SSR HTML | Critical scripts (polyfills) |
| `afterInteractive`  | Injected after client hydration    | Analytics, widgets           |
| `lazyOnload`        | Deferred via `requestIdleCallback` | Non-essential trackers       |

Security [#security]

By default, all `<Script>` components are **blocked** unless you explicitly opt in:

```tsx
// ✅ Allowed
<Script src="..." dangerouslySetScripts />

// ❌ Blocked (logs a security warning)
<Script src="..." />
```

To disable this requirement globally, set `requireDangerouslySetScripts: false` in `jen.config.ts`:

```typescript title="jen.config.ts"
export default {
  requireDangerouslySetScripts: false,
};
```

Inline Scripts [#inline-scripts]

```tsx
<Script id="gtag" strategy="afterInteractive" dangerouslySetScripts>
  {`window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];`}
</Script>
```

> \[!CAUTION]
> The `dangerouslySetScripts` prop exists as a security safeguard. Only enable it for scripts you trust.


# API Routes



Jen.js supports API routes via the `pages/api/` directory. Each file exports HTTP method handlers following the standard Fetch API conventions.

Creating an API Route [#creating-an-api-route]

```typescript title="pages/api/users.ts"
import type { APIRequest, APIResponse, APIHandler } from 'we-jenjs/core/api-router';

export const GET: APIHandler = async (req, res) => {
  const users = await db.getUsers();
  return res.json({ users });
};

export const POST: APIHandler = async (req, res) => {
  const body = req.body as { name: string; email: string };
  const user = await db.createUser(body);
  return res.setStatus(201).json({ user });
};
```

Route Mapping [#route-mapping]

Files in `pages/api/` map to URL paths:

| File                      | Route             |
| ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `pages/api/users.ts`      | `/api/users`      |
| `pages/api/posts.ts`      | `/api/posts`      |
| `pages/api/auth/login.ts` | `/api/auth/login` |

Supported Methods [#supported-methods]

Export any of these HTTP method handlers:

* `GET`
* `POST`
* `PUT`
* `DELETE`
* `PATCH`
* `HEAD`
* `OPTIONS`

APIResponse Builder [#apiresponse-builder]

The `APIResponse` object provides fluent methods:

```typescript
// JSON response
return res.json({ message: 'ok' });

// Text response
return res.text('Hello');

// HTML response
return res.html('<h1>Hello</h1>');

// Custom status
return res.setStatus(404).json({ error: 'Not found' });

// Custom headers
return res.setHeader('X-Custom', 'value').json({ data });

// Empty response
return res.setStatus(204).empty();
```

Request Object [#request-object]

The `APIRequest` extends the standard Fetch `Request` with:

```typescript
interface APIRequest extends Omit<Request, 'body'> {
  query?: Record<string, string | string[]>;  // Parsed query params
  body?: unknown;                              // Parsed request body
}
```


# Data Fetching



Jen.js provides a built-in data loading system that runs exclusively on the server. Export a `load()` or `server()` function from any page to fetch data before rendering.

Basic Usage [#basic-usage]

```tsx title="pages/app.tsx"
import type { LoadContext, LoadResult } from 'we-jenjs/core/data-loader';

export async function load(ctx: LoadContext): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts').then(r => r.json());

  return {
    props: { posts: data },
  };
}

export default function Home({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map(post => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

The `load()` function runs on the server during SSR and its return value is passed as props to your component.

LoadContext [#loadcontext]

The context object provides request information:

```typescript
interface LoadContext {
  url: string;                              // Full request URL
  pathname: string;                         // URL pathname
  params?: Record<string, string>;          // Dynamic route params
  query?: Record<string, string | string[]>; // Query string parameters
  headers?: Headers;                        // Request headers
}
```

LoadResult [#loadresult]

The return object controls rendering behavior:

```typescript
interface LoadResult {
  props: Record<string, unknown>;  // Data passed to the component
  revalidate?: number;             // ISR revalidation time (seconds)
  redirect?: string;               // Redirect URL (307)
  notFound?: boolean;              // Return 404
}
```

Redirects [#redirects]

Return a `redirect` to send the user elsewhere:

```typescript
export async function load(ctx: LoadContext): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const session = await getSession(ctx.headers);

  if (!session) {
    return { props: {}, redirect: '/login' };
  }

  return { props: { user: session.user } };
}
```

Not Found [#not-found]

Return `notFound: true` to trigger a 404 response:

```typescript
export async function load(ctx: LoadContext): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const post = await getPost(ctx.params?.slug);

  if (!post) {
    return { props: {}, notFound: true };
  }

  return { props: { post } };
}
```

ISR Revalidation [#isr-revalidation]

Set `revalidate` to enable [Incremental Static Regeneration](/docs/rendering/isr):

```typescript
export async function load(): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const data = await fetchData();
  return {
    props: { data },
    revalidate: 60, // Re-generate every 60 seconds
  };
}
```

> \[!NOTE]
> `server()` is an alias for `load()`. Both work identically — use whichever name you prefer.


# Cloudflare Workers



Jen.js includes a Cloudflare Workers adapter that compiles your application into a single JavaScript file compatible with the Workers runtime.

Build [#build]

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen build --adapter=cloudflare
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

What Gets Generated [#what-gets-generated]

```
dist/static/
├── cloudflare-worker.js   ← Self-contained Worker bundle
├── index.html
├── about.html
├── sitemap.xml
└── robots.txt
```

Architecture [#architecture]

Cloudflare Workers prohibit filesystem APIs and dynamically-bound WASM imports. The Jen.js adapter handles this by:

1. **Bypassing the Rust WASM RouterMap** — Generates a pure JavaScript `switch` evaluator for route matching
2. **Inlining SSR** — Uses `preact-render-to-string` directly in the Worker
3. **SWC minification** — Optimizes the bundle for V8 edge engines with `module: true, compress: true`

Deploy [#deploy]

Deploy using [Wrangler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/):

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    # Install Wrangler
    npm install -g wrangler

    # Deploy
    wrangler deploy dist/static/cloudflare-worker.js
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    # Install Wrangler
    pnpm add -g wrangler

    # Deploy
    wrangler deploy dist/static/cloudflare-worker.js
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    # Install Wrangler
    yarn global add wrangler

    # Deploy
    wrangler deploy dist/static/cloudflare-worker.js
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    # Install Wrangler
    bun add -g wrangler

    # Deploy
    wrangler deploy dist/static/cloudflare-worker.js
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Configuration [#configuration]

Create a `wrangler.toml` for custom Worker settings:

```toml title="wrangler.toml"
name = "my-jen-app"
main = "dist/static/cloudflare-worker.js"
compatibility_date = "2026-03-01"

[site]
bucket = "./dist/static"
```

> \[!WARNING]
> Dynamic routes using the Rust WASM router are unavailable in Cloudflare Workers. All routing is handled via the compiled JavaScript switch evaluator.

# Vercel



Jen.js includes a built-in Vercel adapter that generates the `.vercel/output` directory structure for instant deployments.

Build [#build]

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen build --adapter=vercel
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen build --adapter=vercel
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen build --adapter=vercel
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen build --adapter=vercel
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

What Gets Generated [#what-gets-generated]

The adapter creates Vercel's [Build Output API v3](https://vercel.com/docs/build-output-api/v3) structure:

```
.vercel/output/
├── config.json
├── static/            ← Pre-rendered HTML, CSS, JS
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── about.html
│   ├── sitemap.xml
│   └── robots.txt
└── functions/
    └── index.func/    ← Serverless lambda wrapper
        └── index.js
```

Features [#features]

* **Static assets** served from the Vercel CDN
* **Serverless function** wrapping the Jen.js SSR engine for dynamic routes
* **Edge Middleware** support (your `middleware.ts` is bundled into the function)
* **SWC minification** targeting V8 edge engines

Deploy [#deploy]

Push to your Git repository connected to Vercel, or deploy manually:

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">

    ```bash
    npm install -g vercel

    # Deploy

    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">

    ```bash
    # Deploy
    vercel --prebuilt
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    # Install Vercel CLI
    yarn global add vercel

    # Deploy
    vercel --prebuilt
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    # Install Vercel CLI
    bun add -g vercel

    # Deploy
    vercel --prebuilt
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

> \[!NOTE]
> The `--prebuilt` flag tells Vercel to use the `.vercel/output` directory that Jen.js already generated, skipping Vercel's own build step.


# Server-Side Rendering



Jen.js uses **streaming server-side rendering** for fast Time to First Byte (TTFB). Pages begin flushing HTML to the browser immediately while components are still rendering.

How It Works [#how-it-works]

The `SsrEngine` renders pages through a pipeline:

1. **Load data** — Execute the page's `load()` function
2. **Build component tree** — `Router` → `ErrorBoundary` → `_app.tsx` → Layouts → Page
3. **Stream HTML** — Use `renderToReadableStream` from `preact-render-to-string/stream`
4. **Inject head** — Font links, route manifest, SSR metrics
5. **Flush response** — `TransformStream` pipes head chunk → component HTML → tail chunk

```
 ┌─ head chunk ─┐  ┌─ component stream ─┐  ┌─ tail chunk ─┐
 │ <!DOCTYPE>   │  │  <div>...</div>     │  │  </body>     │
 │ <head>...</>  │  │  (streamed)         │  │  </html>     │
 └──────────────┘  └────────────────────┘  └─────────────┘
```

Hydration [#hydration]

After the full HTML is streamed, the client-side Preact hydration script boots:

1. Reads `window.__JEN_ROUTE_MANIFEST__` for route definitions
2. Dynamically imports the page component and layouts
3. Calls `hydrate()` on the `#jen-root` container

This enables instant interactivity without re-fetching page data.

Development Server [#development-server]

During development, `jen dev` starts a Vite-powered dev server with:

* Hot Module Replacement (HMR)
* On-demand SSR via `vite.ssrLoadModule()`
* Automatic CSS injection from `style.css` co-located with page components

Production Server [#production-server]

`jen start` runs a production-hardened server with:

* NIST SP 800-44 and OWASP ASVS L1 security headers
* Streaming SSR for all routes
* ISR cache integration
* Static asset serving from `dist/static/`


# Incremental Static Regeneration



Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) lets you serve cached HTML while regenerating pages on a schedule in the background — combining the speed of static with the freshness of SSR.

Enable ISR [#enable-isr]

Add ISR configuration to `jen.config.ts`:

```typescript title="jen.config.ts"
export default {
  isr: {
    enabled: true,
    cacheDir: '.cache/isr',    // Cache storage location
    maxRetries: 3,             // Retry failed regenerations
    retryDelay: 1000,          // Delay between retries (ms)
    globalRevalidate: 300,     // Global fallback TTL (seconds)
  },
};
```

Per-Page Revalidation [#per-page-revalidation]

Set a `revalidate` value in your `load()` function:

```typescript title="pages/blog/app.tsx"
export async function load(): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const posts = await fetchPosts();

  return {
    props: { posts },
    revalidate: 60, // Revalidate every 60 seconds
  };
}
```

How It Works [#how-it-works]

The ISR system follows the **stale-while-revalidate** pattern:

| Cache Status | Behavior                                           |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `MISS`       | Render from scratch, cache the result              |
| `HIT_FRESH`  | Serve cached HTML immediately                      |
| `HIT_STALE`  | Serve cached HTML, trigger background regeneration |

Cache Headers [#cache-headers]

ISR responses include diagnostic headers:

```
X-Cache-Status: HIT_FRESH | HIT_STALE | MISS
X-Cache-Age: 45    (seconds since cached)
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000              (fresh)
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=31536000  (stale)
```

ISR Types [#isr-types]

The ISR system exposes these core types:

```typescript
interface CacheEntry {
  html: string;
  timestamp: number;  // Unix epoch (ms)
}

interface FreshnessResult {
  isFresh: boolean;
  isStale: boolean;
  age: number;        // milliseconds
}

type CacheStatus = 'MISS' | 'HIT_FRESH' | 'HIT_STALE';
```

Storage Providers [#storage-providers]

ISR supports pluggable storage via the `IStorageProvider` interface:

```typescript
interface IStorageProvider {
  get(key: string): Promise<CacheEntry | null>;
  set(key: string, entry: CacheEntry): Promise<void>;
  delete(key: string): Promise<void>;
  exists(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

The default provider uses in-memory storage. A filesystem-backed provider is used in production builds.

> \[!NOTE]
> ISR only caches `GET` requests. Non-GET requests always bypass the cache.


# Static Site Generation



Jen.js can generate a fully static site from your pages during the build step — perfect for hosting on GitHub Pages, S3, Cloudflare Pages, or any static CDN.

Build Command [#build-command]

<Tabs items="[&#x22;npm&#x22;, &#x22;pnpm&#x22;, &#x22;yarn&#x22;, &#x22;bun&#x22;]">
  <Tab value="npm">
    ```bash
    npx jen build
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="pnpm">
    ```bash
    pnpm jen build
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="yarn">
    ```bash
    yarn jen build
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="bun">
    ```bash
    bunx jen build
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

This scans all non-dynamic routes, renders them with Preact, and outputs optimized HTML, CSS, and JS to `dist/static/`.

What Gets Generated [#what-gets-generated]

For each static route, the `StaticSiteGenerator`:

1. Creates a Preact entry file per page (including layout composition)
2. Server-renders the page to HTML with `renderToString`
3. Evaluates `metadata` / `generateMetadata()` for SEO tags
4. Bundles with Vite in production mode (esbuild minification)
5. Injects the route manifest for client hydration

Example Output [#example-output]

```
dist/static/
├── index.html           ← /
├── about/
│   └── index.html       ← /about (if using rollup naming)
├── sitemap.xml           ← Auto-generated
└── robots.txt            ← Auto-generated
```

Automatic SEO Files [#automatic-seo-files]

During build, Jen.js automatically generates:

* **`sitemap.xml`** — Lists all static routes following the [sitemaps.org](https://www.sitemaps.org/) protocol
* **`robots.txt`** — Standard crawler directives pointing to the sitemap

Dynamic Routes [#dynamic-routes]

Dynamic routes (e.g., `[$slug]`) are **excluded** from static generation since their paths are unknown at build time. They are served via SSR or ISR at runtime.

Image Optimization [#image-optimization]

The build pipeline integrates the `jenImageOptimizerPlugin` for Vite, automatically processing local images referenced in components with Sharp for WebP conversion and size optimization.

i18n Static Output [#i18n-static-output]

When [i18n](/docs/i18n) is configured, the build generates separate directories per locale:

```
dist/static/
├── en/
│   ├── index.html
│   └── about.html
└── fr/
    ├── index.html
    └── about.html
```


# Dynamic Routes



Dynamic routes let you create pages that match variable URL segments, like `/blog/:slug` or `/users/:id`.

Convention [#convention]

Wrap the parameter name in `[$...]` as a **folder name**:

```
pages/
└── blog/
    └── [$slug]/
        └── app.tsx      → /blog/:slug
```

The folder `[$slug]` declares a dynamic segment. Any URL matching `/blog/*` will render this page with the parameter value available in the data loader.

Accessing Parameters [#accessing-parameters]

Use the `load()` function to access dynamic parameters:

```tsx title="pages/blog/[$slug]/app.tsx"
import type { LoadContext, LoadResult } from 'we-jenjs/core/data-loader';

export async function load(ctx: LoadContext): Promise<LoadResult> {
  const slug = ctx.params?.slug;
  const post = await fetchPost(slug);

  return {
    props: { post },
  };
}

export default function BlogPost({ post }: { post: Post }) {
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      <div>{post.content}</div>
    </article>
  );
}
```

The `params` object on `LoadContext` contains all extracted dynamic segments from the URL.

Multiple Dynamic Segments [#multiple-dynamic-segments]

You can nest dynamic segments:

```
pages/
└── users/
    └── [$userId]/
        └── posts/
            └── [$postId]/
                └── app.tsx   → /users/:userId/posts/:postId
```

Both `ctx.params.userId` and `ctx.params.postId` are available in `load()`.

> \[!NOTE]
> Dynamic routes are **excluded from static site generation** by default since their paths are only known at runtime. They render via streaming SSR or ISR.


# Routing



Jen.js uses a **file-system based router**. Every directory under `pages/` containing an `app.tsx` (or `app.jsx`) file is automatically registered as a route.

How It Works [#how-it-works]

The `RouteScanner` walks the `pages/` directory at startup and builds a route manifest. This manifest is compiled into a high-performance `RouterMap` backed by a Rust/WASM module for near-instant pattern matching.

```
pages/
├── app.tsx              → /
├── about/
│   └── app.tsx          → /about
├── blog/
│   ├── app.tsx          → /blog
│   └── [$slug]/
│       └── app.tsx      → /blog/:slug
└── dashboard/
    ├── layout.tsx       → shared layout
    ├── app.tsx          → /dashboard
    └── settings/
        └── app.tsx      → /dashboard/settings
```

Route Components [#route-components]

Each `app.tsx` file must export a **default Preact component**:

```tsx title="pages/about/app.tsx"
export default function About() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>About Us</h1>
      <p>Welcome to our site.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Client-Side Navigation [#client-side-navigation]

Jen.js intercepts navigation clicks using the `<Link>` component for smooth, SPA-like transitions without full page reloads:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'we-jenjs/client';

export default function Nav() {
  return (
    <nav>
      <Link href="/">Home</Link>
      <Link href="/about">About</Link>
      <Link href="/blog">Blog</Link>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

The client router fetches the target page and swaps content while preserving layout state. See [Components → Link](/docs/components/link) for details.

Static Route Manifest [#static-route-manifest]

During SSR, the route manifest is injected into the HTML as `window.__JEN_ROUTE_MANIFEST__`, enabling the client router to resolve pages without a server round-trip.


# Layouts



Jen.js supports **cascading layouts** that persist across page navigations — keeping navbars, sidebars, and shared UI mounted.

Layout Files [#layout-files]

Place a `layout.tsx` file in any directory under `pages/`. It wraps all pages in that subtree:

```tsx title="pages/layout.tsx"
export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: any }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <header>My App</header>
      <main>{children}</main>
      <footer>© 2026</footer>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Nesting [#nesting]

Layouts compose automatically based on directory depth:

```
pages/
├── layout.tsx              ← Root layout
├── app.tsx                 ← / (inside root layout)
└── dashboard/
    ├── layout.tsx          ← Dashboard layout
    ├── app.tsx             ← /dashboard (root → dashboard layout)
    └── settings/
        └── app.tsx         ← /dashboard/settings (root → dashboard layout)
```

When a user visits `/dashboard/settings`, both the root layout and the dashboard layout are applied in order.

Global App Shell (`_app.tsx`) [#global-app-shell-_apptsx]

For logic that must wrap **every** page globally (providers, themes, analytics), create a `_app.tsx` in the project root:

```tsx title="_app.tsx"
export default function App({ Component, pageProps, children }: any) {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      {children}
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

The `_app.tsx` receives:

* `Component` — the current page component
* `pageProps` — props from `load()`
* `children` — the pre-composed layout → page tree

Error Boundary (`_error.tsx`) [#error-boundary-_errortsx]

Create `_error.tsx` to catch rendering errors gracefully:

```tsx title="_error.tsx"
export default function ErrorPage({ error }: { error?: Error }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Something went wrong</h1>
      <p>{error?.message || 'An unexpected error occurred.'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

This component renders when a page or layout throws during SSR or client hydration.
